This is an operating-systems course lab (Projects 1–6) that implements a RISC-V bare-metal operating system. The repo spans six incremental projects: a bootloader, a simple cooperative kernel, a preemptive kernel with SMP, an interactive OS with process management and IPC, a virtual-memory-enabled kernel with demand paging, a device-driver layer with network support, and a file system. Entire subsystems have been removed and must be re-implemented.

Your working directory is `/workspace`. The project code is already present in seven subdirectories: `Project1-Bootloader`, `Project2-A_Simple_Kernel_Part1`, `Project2-A_Simple_Kernel_Part2`, `Project3-Interactive_OS_and_Process_Management`, `Project4-Virtual_Memory_Management`, `Project5-Device_Driver`, and `Project6-File_System`.

Implement the following modules:

The following modules need to be implemented or substantially built out. All stubbed function bodies contain `/* TODO: implement */`.

Bootloader Image Builder (`Project1-Bootloader/createimage.c`): The host-side tool that reads ELF binaries and writes a bootable disk image. Two functions handle segment writing and OS size recording. (~1 file, 2 functions to implement)

Part 1 Scheduler & Locking (`Project2-A_Simple_Kernel_Part1/kernel/sched/sched.c`, `kernel/locking/lock.c`): The cooperative round-robin scheduler, task blocking/unblocking primitives, and mutex lock acquire/release. (~2 files, 5 functions to implement)

Part 2 Scheduler & Synchronisation (`Project2-A_Simple_Kernel_Part2/kernel/`): The preemptive priority-based scheduler with ready-queue management, priority-based task selection, timer expiration checking, mutex locking, binary semaphore operations, and futex wait/wakeup with hash-based node management. (~5 files, 9 functions to implement)

Process Management & IPC (`Project3-Interactive_OS_and_Process_Management/kernel/`): Multi-core scheduler with process lifecycle management (spawn, exit, kill, waitpid), priority-based scheduling with CPU affinity masks, binary semaphore tracking, and a mailbox-based inter-process communication system for sending and receiving messages with blocking semantics. (~4 files, 12 functions to implement)

Virtual Memory Management (`Project4-Virtual_Memory_Management/kernel/mm/mm.c`, `kernel/sched/sched.c`): SV39 three-level page table initialisation and teardown, user page allocation with NRU page replacement, swap-to-disk eviction, demand-paging page fault handling, shared memory mapping/unmapping, process creation/execution with ELF loading, and process termination with resource cleanup. (~2 files, 13 functions to implement)

Device Driver Layer (`Project5-Device_Driver/drivers/net.c`, `kernel/mm/mm.c`, `kernel/sched/sched.c`): Network packet send/receive with poll and interrupt modes, IRQ mode switching, plus the full virtual memory and scheduler subsystems carried forward from Project 4 with additional page-helper functionality. (~3 files, 18 functions to implement)

File System (`Project6-File_System/kernel/fs/`): A complete on-disk file system with superblock/bitmap-based allocation, inode and block management (alloc, free), directory operations (mkdir, rmdir, ls, cd), hard/soft linking, file operations (touch, cat, fopen, fread, fwrite), plus the full scheduler and virtual memory subsystems from Project 5. (~6 files, 24 functions to implement)

The tests also depend on these signatures and entry points:

The following functions are called or inspected directly by the test suite. You must implement them with these exact signatures:

`static void write_segment(Elf64_Phdr phdr, FILE *fp, FILE *img, int *nbytes)` — writes an ELF segment to a disk image with 512-byte alignment
`static void write_os_size(int nbytes, FILE *img)` — writes the OS sector count at offset 508 in the image
`void do_scheduler(void)` (P2A) — cooperative round-robin scheduler
`void do_block(list_node_t *pcb_node, list_head *queue)` (P2A) — moves a PCB to a block queue
`void do_unblock(list_node_t *pcb_node)` (P2A) — moves a PCB back to the ready queue
`void do_mutex_lock_acquire(mutex_lock_t *lock)` (P2A, P2B) — acquires a mutex with blocking
`void do_mutex_lock_release(mutex_lock_t *lock)` (P2A, P2B) — releases a mutex and wakes waiters
`void scheduler(void)` (P2B, P3, P4, P5, P6) — preemptive priority-based scheduler
`list_node_t* max_priority_node(void)` (P2B, P3, P4, P5, P6) — selects the highest-priority ready task
`pid_t do_spawn(task_info_t *task, void *arg, spawn_mode_t mode)` (P3) — creates a new process
`void do_exit()` (P3, P4, P5, P6) — handles process exit and resource cleanup
`int do_kill(pid_t pid)` (P3, P4, P5, P6) — terminates a process by PID
`int do_waitpid(pid_t pid, ...)` (P3, P4, P5, P6) — waits for a child process to exit
`ptr_t alloc_user_page(uint8_t pin, PTE *pgtable)` (P4, P5, P6) — allocates a physical page for user space
`ptr_t selete_page(void)` (P4, P5, P6) — NRU page replacement to select a victim page
`void write_to_sd(ptr_t pa)` (P4, P5, P6) — evicts a page to disk swap space
`PTE* init_page_table(void)` (P4, P5, P6) — creates a three-level SV39 page table for a new process
`void free_process_user_page(PTE *pgdir)` (P4, P5, P6) — recursively frees all pages owned by a process
`uintptr_t shm_page_get(int key)` (P4, P5, P6) — maps a shared memory page into the current process
`void shm_page_dt(uintptr_t addr)` (P4, P5, P6) — unmaps a shared memory page
`void handle_page_fault(regs_context_t *regs, uint64_t stval, uint64_t cause)` (P4, P5, P6) — demand-paging page fault handler
`long do_net_recv(uintptr_t addr, size_t length, int num_packet, size_t *frLength)` (P5) — receives network packets
`void do_net_send(uintptr_t addr, size_t length)` (P5) — sends a network packet
`void do_net_irq_mode(int mode)` (P5) — switches between poll and interrupt modes
`uint16_t alloc_inode()` (P6) — allocates a free inode from the bitmap
`uint32_t alloc_block()` (P6) — allocates a free block from the bitmap
`void free_inode(uint16_t inode_id)` (P6) — frees an inode in the bitmap
`void free_block(uint32_t block_id)` (P6) — frees a block in the bitmap
`int mkfs(int print)` (P6) — initialises the file system superblock and root directory
`int do_mkdir(char *dirname)` (P6) — creates a new directory
`int do_rmdir(char *dirname)` (P6) — removes a directory
`int do_ls(char *dirname, int mode, int *print_location_y)` (P6) — lists directory contents
`int do_cd(char *dirname)` (P6) — changes the current working directory
`int do_link(char *filename, char *newfile, int mode)` (P6) — creates hard or soft links
`int do_touch(char *filename)` (P6) — creates a new empty file
`int do_cat(char *filename, char *buffer)` (P6) — reads file contents into a buffer
`int do_fopen(char *filename, int access)` (P6) — opens a file and returns a file descriptor
`int do_fread(int fd, char *buffer, int size)` (P6) — reads data from an open file
`int do_fwrite(int fd, char *buffer, int size)` (P6) — writes data to an open file
`int do_mbox_open(char *name)` (P3) — opens or creates a named mailbox
`int do_mbox_send(int mailbox_id, void *msg, int msg_length)` (P3) — sends a message to a mailbox
`int do_mbox_recv(int mailbox_id, void *msg, int msg_length)` (P3) — receives a message from a mailbox
`void binsem_op(int binsem_id, int op)` (P2B, P3) — performs lock/unlock on a binary semaphore
`futex_node_t* get_node(volatile uint64_t *val_addr, int create)` (P2B) — looks up or creates a futex node
`void futex_wait(volatile uint64_t *val_addr, uint64_t val)` (P2B) — blocks on a futex if value matches
`void futex_wakeup(volatile uint64_t *val_addr, int num_wakeup)` (P2B) — wakes tasks blocked on a futex
`void timer_check(void)` (P2B) — checks expired timers and invokes callbacks
`pid_t do_exec(const char *file_name, int argc, char *argv[], spawn_mode_t mode)` (P4, P5, P6) — loads and executes an ELF binary as a new process
`uintptr_t alloc_page_helper(uintptr_t va, uintptr_t pgdir)` (P5, P6) — allocates a page and maps it at a virtual address

addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

#!/bin/bash
# Build a project subtree in a scratch directory so the repo stays clean.
#
# The checked-in host tools (elf2char/createimage/generateMapping) are mode
# 644 in git and the Makefile hard-codes a cross prefix that does not exist in
# this container, so we copy the tree out and fix both there.  gcc >= 10 also
# defaults to -fno-common, which trips over the generated user_programs.h; the
# original lab toolchain was older, hence -fcommon.
#
# usage: agent_tests/build.sh <ProjectDir> [make target...]
set -u

PROJ="$1"; shift
SRC="/workspace/$PROJ"
DST="/tmp/b/$(echo "$PROJ" | cut -c1-8)"

[ -d "$SRC" ] || { echo "no such project: $SRC"; exit 2; }

rm -rf "$DST"
mkdir -p /tmp/b
cp -a "$SRC" "$DST" || exit 2
chmod +x "$DST"/elf2char "$DST"/createimage "$DST"/generateMapping 2>/dev/null

sed -i 's/^CROSS_PREFIX = .*/CROSS_PREFIX = riscv64-linux-gnu-/' "$DST/Makefile"
sed -i 's/^\(CFLAGS = .*\)$/\1 -fcommon/' "$DST/Makefile"
sed -i 's/^\(USER_CFLAGS = .*\)$/\1 -fcommon/' "$DST/Makefile"

cd "$DST" || exit 2
timeout 1200 make "${@:-main}" 2>&1

ENTRY(enable_interrupt)
  li t0, SR_SIE
  csrs CSR_SSTATUS, t0
  jr ra
ENDPROC(enable_interrupt)

ENTRY(disable_interrupt)
  li t0, SR_SIE
  csrc CSR_SSTATUS, t0
  jr ra
ENDPROC(disable_interrupt)

ENTRY(enable_sum)
  li t0, SR_SUM
  csrs CSR_SSTATUS, t0
  jr ra
ENDPROC(enable_sum)

ENTRY(disable_sum)
  li t0, SR_SUM
  csrc CSR_SSTATUS, t0
  jr ra
ENDPROC(disable_sum)

ENTRY(ret_from_exception)
  ld tp, current_cpu_running
  call unlock_kernel
  RESTORE_CONTEXT

  csrrw tp, CSR_SSCRATCH, tp
  bnez tp, to_user
to_kernel:
  csrrw tp, CSR_SSCRATCH, tp
  ld sp, PCB_KERNEL_SP(tp)
  j restore_sp_done
to_user:
  ld sp, PCB_USER_SP(tp)
restore_sp_done:
  sret
ENDPROC(ret_from_exception)

ENTRY(exception_handler_entry)
  /* use kernel stack to handle exception */
  csrrw tp, CSR_SSCRATCH, tp
  bnez tp, from_user

from_kernel:
  csrrw tp, CSR_SSCRATCH, tp
  j store_sp_done
from_user:
  sd sp, PCB_USER_SP(tp)
  ld sp, PCB_KERNEL_SP(tp)
store_sp_done:

  SAVE_CONTEXT
  /* 
   * Disable user-mode memory access as it should only be set in the actual user copy routines.
   * Disable the FPU to detect illegal usage of floating point in kernel space.
   */
  li t0, SR_SUM | SR_FS
  csrc sstatus, t0

  /* load the global pointer */
  .option push
  .option norelax
  la gp, __global_pointer$
  .option pop

  call lock_kernel
  /* 
   * load ret_from_exception into $ra
   * so that we can return to ret_from_exception
   * when interrupt_helper complete.
   */
  la ra, ret_from_exception
  
  /* call interrupt_helper and pass parameters for it */
  mv a0, sp
  csrr a1, CSR_STVAL
  csrr a2, CSR_SCAUSE

#!/bin/bash
# Host-side functional tests for the kernel subsystems implemented in this repo.
#
# Kernel code is compiled natively (with small shims under hostshim/ standing in
# for the RISC-V specific headers) and driven directly, so the scheduling,
# synchronisation, IPC and file-system logic can be executed and asserted on
# without a board or an emulator.
set -u

cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." || exit 1
ROOT=$(pwd)
SHIM="$ROOT/agent_tests/hostshim"
OUT=$(mktemp -d)
fail=0

run_case() {
    local name=$1; shift
    if ! gcc -g -O0 -o "$OUT/$name" "$@" 2>"$OUT/$name.log"; then
        echo "[$name] COMPILE FAILED"
        sed -n '1,40p' "$OUT/$name.log"
        fail=1
        return
    fi
    if ! timeout 60 "$OUT/$name"; then
        echo "[$name] RUN FAILED"
        fail=1
    fi
}

P2A="$ROOT/Project2-A_Simple_Kernel_Part1"
run_case p2a_sched \
    "$ROOT/agent_tests/p2a_sched_test.c" \
    "$P2A/kernel/sched/sched.c" "$P2A/kernel/locking/lock.c" \
    -I"$SHIM" -I"$P2A/include" -I"$P2A/drivers" -I"$P2A/arch/riscv/include"

# get_ticks() reads the RISC-V `time` CSR, which the host cannot execute.  Swap
# just that one read for a counter the test drives; timer_check() -- the code
# actually under test -- is compiled verbatim.
host_time_c() {
    python3 - "$1" "$2" <<'PY'
import sys
src = open(sys.argv[1]).read()
asm = '''    __asm__ __volatile__(
        "rdtime %0"
        : "=r"(time_elapsed));'''
assert asm in src, "get_ticks() no longer looks the way the test expects"
src = src.replace(asm, "    time_elapsed = host_get_ticks();")
src = "extern unsigned long host_get_ticks(void);\n" + src
open(sys.argv[2], "w").write(src)
PY
}

P2B="$ROOT/Project2-A_Simple_Kernel_Part2"
if [ -f "$ROOT/agent_tests/p2b_sched_test.c" ]; then
    host_time_c "$P2B/kernel/sched/time.c" "$OUT/p2b_time.c"
    run_case p2b_sched \
        "$ROOT/agent_tests/p2b_sched_test.c" \
        "$P2B/kernel/sched/sched.c" "$P2B/kernel/locking/lock.c" \
        "$P2B/kernel/locking/futex.c" "$P2B/kernel/locking/binsem.c" \
        "$OUT/p2b_time.c" \
        -I"$SHIM" -I"$P2B/include" -I"$P2B/drivers" -I"$P2B/arch/riscv/include"
fi

P3="$ROOT/Project3-Interactive_OS_and_Process_Management"
if [ -f "$ROOT/agent_tests/p3_proc_test.c" ]; then
    host_time_c "$P3/kernel/sched/time.c" "$OUT/p3_time.c"
    run_case p3_proc \
        "$ROOT/agent_tests/p3_proc_test.c" \
        "$P3/kernel/sched/sched.c" "$P3/kernel/syscall/mailbox.c" \
        "$P3/kernel/locking/binsem.c" "$P3/libs/string.c" "$OUT/p3_time.c" \
        -I"$SHIM" -I"$P3/include" -I"$P3/drivers" -I"$P3/arch/riscv/include"
fi

P6="$ROOT/Project6-File_System"
if [ -f "$ROOT/agent_tests/p6_fs_test.c" ]; then
    run_case p6_fs \
        "$ROOT/agent_tests/p6_fs_test.c" \
        "$P6/kernel/fs/fs.c" "$P6/kernel/fs/file.c" \
        -I"$SHIM" -I"$P6/include" -I"$P6/drivers" -I"$P6/arch/riscv/include"
fi

rm -rf "$OUT"
if [ "$fail" -ne 0 ]; then
    echo "SOME TESTS FAILED"
    exit 1
fi
echo "ALL HOST TESTS PASSED"
=== hostshim/type.h ===
/* Host-side stand-in for include/type.h.
 *
 * The kernel header rolls its own fixed-width typedefs with gcc mode
 * attributes, which collide with glibc's <stdint.h> when the same translation
 * unit needs both (the unit tests need malloc/printf/ucontext).  This shim
 * exposes the identical set of names on top of <stdint.h> so the kernel
 * sources compile unchanged natively.
 */
#ifndef INCLUDE_TYPE_H_
#define INCLUDE_TYPE_H_

#include <stdint.h>
#include <stddef.h>

#ifndef NULL
#define NULL (void *)0
#endif

#ifndef TRUE
#define TRUE  1
#define FALSE 0
#endif

typedef int32_t pid_t;
typedef uint64_t reg_t;
typedef uint64_t ptr_t;

#endif

/* Host stand-in for Project6-File_System/include/assert.h.
 *
 * Neither <stdio.h> nor <stdlib.h> can be included from here: the kernel's
 * own stdio.h shadows glibc's, and glibc's stdlib.h contradicts the kernel's
 * atoi() prototype.  The two entry points are declared by hand. */
#ifndef ASSERT_H
#define ASSERT_H

extern int printf(const char *fmt, ...);
extern void abort(void);

#define assert(cond)                                                    \
    {                                                                   \
        if (!(cond)) {                                                  \
            printf("kernel assertion failed at %s:%d (%s)\n",           \
                   __FILE__, __LINE__, __FUNCTION__);                   \
            abort();                                                    \
        }                                                               \
    }

#endif
EOF

p='agent_tests/run_tests.sh'
s=open(p).read()
old = '''P6="$ROOT/Project6-File_System"
if [ -f "$ROOT/agent_tests/p6_fs_test.c" ]; then
    run_case p6_fs \\

        -I"$SHIM" -I"$P6/include" -I"$P6/drivers" -I"$P6/arch/riscv/include"
fi
'''
new = '''# The file system caches live at a fixed kernel virtual address that a host
# process cannot map.  Relocating just that window to the matching physical
# address (which the test mmaps) keeps every struct, constant and offset in
# os/fs.h exactly as the kernel sees them.
host_fs_h() {
    mkdir -p "$2/os"
    python3 - "$1" "$2/os/fs.h" <<'PY'
import sys
src = open(sys.argv[1]).read()
assert "0xffffffc05f0" in src, "the fs cache is no longer where the test expects"
open(sys.argv[2], "w").write(src.replace("0xffffffc05f0", "0x000000005f0"))
PY
}

P6="$ROOT/Project6-File_System"
if [ -f "$ROOT/agent_tests/p6_fs_test.c" ]; then
    host_fs_h "$P6/include/os/fs.h" "$OUT/p6inc"
    run_case p6_fs \\
        "$ROOT/agent_tests/p6_fs_test.c" \\

        -I"$OUT/p6inc" -I"$ROOT/agent_tests/hostshim_fs" -I"$SHIM" \\
        -I"$P6/include" -I"$P6/drivers"
fi
'''
assert old in s
s = s.replace(old, new)
open(p,'w').write(s)
print("patched")
PY

#!/bin/bash
# Host-side functional tests for the kernel subsystems implemented in this repo.
#
# Kernel code is compiled natively (with small shims under hostshim/ standing in
# for the RISC-V specific headers) and driven directly, so the scheduling,
# synchronisation, IPC and file-system logic can be executed and asserted on
# without a board or an emulator.
set -u

cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." || exit 1
ROOT=$(pwd)
SHIM="$ROOT/agent_tests/hostshim"
OUT=$(mktemp -d)
fail=0

run_case() {
    local name=$1; shift
    if ! gcc -g -O0 -o "$OUT/$name" "$@" 2>"$OUT/$name.log"; then
        echo "[$name] COMPILE FAILED"
        sed -n '1,40p' "$OUT/$name.log"
        fail=1
        return
    fi
    if ! timeout 60 "$OUT/$name"; then
